title: Write and Solve Equations Using Addition or Subtraction
objective: I can solve one-step addition and subtraction equations using inverse operations.
model: balance scale (and tape diagram): do the same inverse operation on both pans, then check by substituting

widgets.component: warm-up: 'three times a number', 'seven less than', 'a number plus 12' as equations
widgets.root: Identical to the lesson's warm-up (8-1 translation); keys 3n = 21, n − 7 = 18, n + 12 = 30 verified.

widgets.component: solve x + 9 = 15, y − 7 = 20, n + 15 = 42, m − 11 = 25; 'subtract 6 from only the left side' error
widgets.root: Keys 6, 27, 27, 36 right; the error's wrong step is e=2 (x + 6 − 6 = 14 leaves the right side unchanged).

widgets.component: 'Use the number line to solve x + 8 = 20. Start at 20 and count back 8'
widgets.root: The stem states the whole method ('Start at 20 and count back 8'), so the student only slides a marker to 12; no equation is written, no inverse operation chosen, and the number line is not the lesson's model (balance scale, tape diagram).
widgets.replacement: Replace with a tape/number-line item where x is the hidden jump: draw 0..25, an arrow of length 8 ending at 20 from an unmarked start, and ask the student to place x and then pick the equation and the inverse step (x + 8 = 20, subtract 8). Remove 'Start at 20 and count back 8'. Traps to name: placing 28 (added 8), placing 20, placing 8.

widgets.component: shirt $d with a $15 discount costs $38; sort six equations by add-to or subtract-from both sides; arithmetic slip in 28 + 13
widgets.root: Key $53 (d − 15 = 38), all six sort cards and the error's wrong step (e=3, 28 + 13 = 31) verified.

widgets.component: generated: story to equation, solve x + a = b and x − a = b with whole numbers, decimals
widgets.root: Ran 300 seeds x 4 levels: every 'Solve x ± a = b' key recomputed (0 mismatches); L1-L3 stories give one add/subtract relation with an unknown start or part.

widgets.where: Practice 4.7; Challenge 3.1-3.2 (act:balance form add L2, L3, L4)
widgets.component: choose the inverse tile and apply it to both pans until the bag is alone
widgets.root: Real model of 'same operation on both sides': every tile changes both pans, the inverse, flipped and wrong-family tiles are offered, decimals and fractions at L3-L4 stay legal.

widgets.component: 'Which operation undoes addition?' and 'Check: does 7.5 work?'
widgets.root: 5.2 is recall whose answer ('Subtraction') is evident from the lesson's wording. 5.3 is the hiker Connect check with its scenario removed: no equation is in the stem, it depends on 5.1's answer, and one choice reads 'Only if the trail is 11 miles' for a trail the page never mentions.
widgets.replacement: 5.2: replace with an act:sort or match of six equations to the first step (add or subtract), as Challenge 3.3 does. 5.3: write the equation in the stem ('A hiker has walked d miles of a 12-mile trail with 4.5 miles left: d + 4.5 = 12. Does d = 7.5 work? Substitute.') and drop the 'trail is 11 miles' option.

widgets.root: Keys 7.5, 6.3, 14.5, 40 recomputed; distractors are the add-instead-of-subtract and unchanged-number results.

widgets.component: solve m + 40 = 99, race distance run, decimal and fraction one-step equations
widgets.root: Same generator checks as Practice §4; L3 decimals (e.g. k + 5.7 = 14.4 gives 8.7) recomputed.

widgets.component: two-change stories ('gave 13 stickers, then got 10, now 41') and 'Solve 1/5 = n − 7/10'
widgets.root: 99 of 300 L4 draws (33%) are a two-change chain, x − 13 + 10 = 41, which is a two-step equation; the lesson's objective, worked example and every other studio item are one-step. A further 11 draws are plain subtraction word problems with no unknown to isolate ('128 signed up, 90 turned in, how many are missing').
widgets.replacement: Drop the chain variant from solveAddSub L4 (or give it as 'net change' only after the student writes the single one-step equation x − 3 = 41). Replace with L4 content that stays one-step but harder: fraction or hundredths change on one side, an unknown on the right ('1/5 = n − 7/10'), and 'which equation has the same solution as...' items.

formulaOrder.formula: x + a = b → x = b − a; x − a = b → x = b + a

typography: Practice 1.1-1.3 print division as 'n / 3', 'n / 7', 'n / 12' while the generated items and the balance scale print '÷'.
